title: Articles
tagline: Year 1 Foundation — A, an, the and when to use no article

introduction.overview: Articles are small words placed before nouns: a, an and the. A and an are indefinite articles used for one non-specific item. The is the definite article used for a specific item that the speaker and listener both know. Sometimes no article is needed. Although articles are tiny, they are a regular topic in fill-in-the-blank and error-spotting questions because the rules depend on sound, not spelling, and on whether a noun is specific, countable or unique.
introduction.placementRelevance: Article questions are commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds, and article errors are among the most common mistakes in written English.
introduction.realWorldContext: Emails, resumes and product descriptions look polished or careless depending on small choices like "an MBA degree" versus "a MBA degree".

learningObjectives: Choose between a and an by the first sound, not the first letter
Use the for specific and unique things
Recognise when no article is needed
Handle names of rivers, mountains, countries and institutions
Use articles with uncountable and abstract nouns correctly

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A noun can be singular or plural, countable or uncountable. A and an go only with singular countable nouns.

coreDefinitions: Indefinite article (a, an): refers to any one member of a class. Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
Definite article (the): refers to a particular, known or unique person or thing.
Zero article (no article): used with plural and uncountable nouns in a general sense, most proper names and some fixed expressions.
Consonant sound: a sound like /b/, /k/, /y/ or /w/ even when the spelling begins with a vowel letter (university, one, European).
Vowel sound: a sound like /a/, /e/, /i/, /o/, /u/ even when the spelling begins with a consonant letter (hour, honest, MBA).
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The choice of a or an is purely about how the next word sounds. If it starts with a vowel sound, use an; if it starts with a consonant sound, use a. The choice of the depends on whether the listener can tell which one you mean.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Say the next word aloud. "Umbrella" starts with an /u/ vowel sound, so an umbrella. "University" starts with a /yoo/ sound (like a y), so a university. "Hour" has a silent h, so an hour.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: A or an
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: a + consonant sound;  an + vowel sound
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: an umbrella, a university, an hour, a European

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Letters read aloud
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: an MBA, an MS, an SQL query, a UFO, a one-day match
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Check the sound of the letter name or the word.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Use of "the"
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Unique things (the sun, the moon, the earth), superlatives (the best), rivers (the Ganga), mountain ranges (the Himalayas), musical instruments (the guitar), and things already mentioned

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: No article
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Plural or uncountable nouns in a general sense, abstract nouns, languages, meals, most countries and cities
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Honesty is the best policy. We have dinner at nine.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Fixed expressions with institutions
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: go to school / college / hospital / church (for the usual purpose) takes no article
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: If you refer to the building, use the.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: He goes to school by bus.

mainNarrative: The basic rule for a and an depends on sound. The letters a, e, i, o, u usually begin a vowel sound (an apple, an egg, an idea), but not always. University, uniform, European and one begin with a /y/ or /w/ consonant sound, so we say a university, a European, a one-day match. Honest, hour and heir begin with a silent h, so we say an honest girl, an hour, an heir.
For abbreviations, use the sound of the first letter name. MBA is read "em-bee-ay", so an MBA; MS is "em-ess", so an MS; UFO is "yoo-ef-oh", so a UFO.

Use the for things that are unique (the sun, the equator), for superlatives (the best player), for rivers, oceans and mountain ranges (the Ganga, the Pacific, the Himalayas), and for musical instruments (play the guitar). Also use the for something already mentioned: "I saw a dog. The dog was barking."

Do not use an article with plural or uncountable nouns used in a general sense (Honesty is the best policy; Books are friends), with languages (She speaks Telugu), with meals (We have dinner at nine), or with most names of countries, cities and individual mountains.

Institutions such as school, college, hospital and church take no article when used for their usual purpose: "He goes to school by bus" (as a student). If you mean the building, use the: "He went to the school to meet the principal."

deepDiveAspects.title: "The" before adjectives used as nouns
deepDiveAspects.content: The + an adjective can mean a group of people: the rich, the poor, the young. These take a plural verb. "The rich are not always happy."

deepDiveAspects.title: Hotel and building names
deepDiveAspects.content: Many names of hotels, theatres, cinemas and landmarks take the: the Taj Mahal Hotel, the Red Fort. Names of most individual people, cities and companies do not.

problemVariations.description: Choose by the sound of the next word.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: He goes to ___ school by bus.

solvedExamples.title: A or an by sound
solvedExamples.question: Fill in the blanks: (a) She is ___ honest girl. (b) He is studying in ___ university. (c) He waited for ___ hour.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Decide by the first sound of the next word.

steps.title: honest
steps.explanation: The h is silent, so the word begins with the vowel sound /o/. Use an.

steps.title: university
steps.explanation: The word begins with the sound /yoo/ (a consonant sound). Use a.

steps.title: hour
steps.explanation: The h is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound. Use an.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: a/an follow the sound, not the spelling.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Choosing "a" for honest and hour because they begin with the letter h.

solvedExamples.title: The with unique items and instruments
solvedExamples.question: Fill in the blanks with a, an, the or no article: (a) ___ sun rises in the east. (b) She plays ___ guitar. (c) ___ Himalayas are in the north.
givenInfo: (a) unique body, (b) musical instrument, (c) mountain range
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Use the for unique things, instruments and mountain ranges.

steps.title: sun
steps.explanation: There is only one sun, so the sun.

steps.title: guitar
steps.explanation: Musical instruments take the: the guitar.

steps.title: Himalayas
steps.explanation: A mountain range takes the: the Himalayas.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: All three are specific or unique things.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Leaving out the before a range or instrument.

solvedExamples.title: No article
solvedExamples.question: Fill in the blank: "___ honesty is the best policy." (a / an / the / no article)
givenInfo: Abstract noun used in a general sense
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Abstract nouns used generally take no article.

steps.title: Identify the noun type
steps.explanation: Honesty is an abstract noun used in a general statement.

steps.title: Apply the rule
steps.explanation: Abstract nouns used in general take no article.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The sentence speaks of honesty in general, not a particular instance of it.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Adding "the" because the sentence feels formal.

shortcutMethods.title: Say it aloud

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Memorise a long list of exceptions to a/an.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Say the next word aloud. A vowel sound takes an; a consonant sound takes a. For the, ask: do both speaker and listener know exactly which one?

rulesForApplication: a university, a European, a one-rupee coin (consonant sound).
an hour, an honest man, an MBA, an SQL query (vowel sound).
Use the with rivers, mountain ranges, oceans, superlatives and instruments.
No article with abstract or plural nouns in a general sense, languages and meals.

commonMistakes.mistake: Choosing by letter instead of sound
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Say the word aloud before choosing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving out the with rivers and ranges
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Use the with rivers, oceans, ranges and groups of islands.
Use no article with abstract nouns used generally.
Use "a piece of information" or "some advice".

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: If the next word starts with a vowel letter, check its sound before choosing; this removes two options at once.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Article blanks are among the quickest grammar questions. Answer them immediately and move on.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Placement tests like exceptions such as "an MBA", "a university" and "the Himalayas".

summaryBullets: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
Use the for unique things, superlatives, rivers, ranges, instruments.
No article for general plurals, abstract and uncountable nouns.
MBA → an; university → a; hour → an.
Institutions for their purpose: no article.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I say why we write "an hour" and "a university"?
Can I choose the right article for the Ganga, the Himalayas, the best player?
Can I explain why "Honesty is the best policy" has no article before honesty?
